title: Organize Automation with Roles
objective: Extract coherent tasks, handlers, files, templates, and defaults into a reusable role.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 14 - Roles
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A role packages one responsibility behind a conventional directory structure. Ansible discovers tasks/main.yml, handlers/main.yml, defaults/main.yml, files, templates, and metadata without custom loading code.

The calling play becomes a readable composition of roles. Public configuration belongs in defaults because callers can override it; hard-to-override internal constants belong in vars only when necessary.
Extract a role when a unit of configuration has a clear purpose and reuse boundary—not simply because a playbook has become long. Roles should remain testable and independently understandable.
explanation.rule: One role should own one coherent system responsibility and expose intentional defaults.

examples.title: Working design or automation artifact
examples.code:
roles:
  webserver:
    tasks: tasks/main.yml
    handlers: handlers/main.yml
    defaults: defaults/main.yml
    templates: templates/
examples.note: Read the structure, predict its effect, then adapt it in the assignment and terminal mission.

checks.question: Where should user-overridable role settings normally live?

feedback.correct: Correct—this matches the demonstrated workflow and keeps the automation explicit.
feedback.incorrect: Review the rule of thumb and the relevant video checkpoint before continuing.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Extract coherent tasks, handlers, files, templates, and defaults into a reusable role.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.
